COLLEGE OF THE ENVIRONMENT & LIFE SCIENCES BA -Sustainable Food Systems, effective Fall 2026 Appendix B A BA in Sustainable Food Systems is ideal for students who wish to pursue a degree in food systems in the context of a liberal arts education.
Because the study and practice of food systems intersects with a wide range of other disciplines, the major is also ideal for those who wish to combine interdisciplinary training in food systems with a complementary major.
Students completing the program will graduate with the skills and knowledge needed to contribute to the development of sustainable, equitable, and resilient food systems from local to global scales.
The major allows participants to explore diverse aspects of the food supply chain from production to processing/distribution to consumption to waste management and recovery, with an emphasis on systems thinking, food system policy, and social, cultural, and political context.

By the time of degree completion, students will be uniquely positioned to enter the workforce in the growing field of sustainable food systems or to pursue opportunities in graduate education or research addressing the challenges of securing access to safe and affordable food for a growing population.
SFS BA students will pursue a curriculum offering breadth across the natural and social sciences and the arts and humanities.
The program entails a total of 120 credits, 30 credits of which must be in courses at the 300 level or above, including: A core sequence emphasizing an interdisciplinary and systems-approach to sustainable food systems.
Required courses include AFS/AVS/PLS 132G, an economics course (to choose from ECN 201, EEC 105, or INE 149), HSS/PSY 130G, NUT 207, one course in sustainability (3 credits minimum, to choose from SUS 102, SAF 305, COM/SUS 108G, COM/SUS 315, COM/SUS 460, and other relevant courses), APG/GWS/SOC 308, SAF 383, and one course in sustainable production (3 credits minimum, to choose from AFS 105G/106, AVS 101/102, or PLS 150).
A minimum of two electives related to food systems at the 300 level or above (6 credits minimum).

A robust capstone experience in which students master the ability to address the complex challenges in the area of sustainable food systems through experiential learning in interdisciplinary teams.
Students are required to take a total of six credits, including three credits of internship or special project and an additional three credits in another capstone course.
Current examples of capstone courses include AFS 440, PLS 385, and SAF 400G.
Compared to the BS in SFS, the BA allows students greater flexibility in selecting courses relevant to their specific interests.
In addition, students may have more flexibility in combining this major with a complementary major in another subject to gain greater breadth of experience they can apply to their future careers.

Kingston No Initiation Date Fall 2026 Program Description 9 First Degree Date Fall 2026 A BA in Sustainable Food Systems is ideal for students who wish to pursue a degree in food systems in the context of a liberal arts education.
Because the study and practice of food systems intersects with a wide range of other disciplines, the major is also ideal for those who wish to combine interdisciplinary training in food systems with a complementary major.
Students completing the program will graduate with the skills and knowledge needed to contribute to the development of sustainable, equitable, and resilient food systems from local to global scales.

The major allows participants to explore diverse aspects of the food supply chain from production to processing/distribution to consumption to waste management and recovery, with an emphasis on systems thinking, food system policy, and social, cultural, and political context.
By the time of degree completion, students will be uniquely positioned to enter the workforce in the growing field of sustainable food systems or to pursue opportunities in graduate education or research addressing the challenges of securing access to safe and affordable food for a growing population.
SFS BA students will pursue a curriculum offering breadth across the natural and social sciences and the arts and humanities.
The program entails a total of 120 credits, 30 credits of which must be in courses at the 300 level or above, including: A core sequence emphasizing an interdisciplinary and systems-approach to sustainable food systems.

Required courses include AFS/ AVS/PLS 132G, an economics course (to choose from ECN 201, EEC 105, or INE 149), HSS/PSY 130G, NUT 207, one course in sustainability (3 credits minimum, to choose from SUS 102, SAF 305, COM/SUS 108G, COM/SUS 315, COM/SUS 460, and other relevant courses), APG/GWS/SOC 308, SAF 383, and one course in sustainable production (3 credits minimum, to choose from AFS 1058/106, AVS 101/102, or PLS 150).
A minimum of two electives related to food systems at the 300 level or above (6 credits minimum).
A robust capstone experience in which students master the ability to address the complex challenges in the area of sustainable food systems through experiential learning in interdisciplinary teams.
Students are required to take a total of six credits, including three credits of internship or special project and an additional three credits in another capstone course.
Current examples of capstone courses include AFS 440, PLS 385, and SAF 400G.
